8	QUESTIONS BY MR. FALK:


Q: State your name, please.
A: Connie Rickert.

Q: And how do you spell your last name, for the court reporter?
A: R-I-C-K-E-R-T.

Q: What is your current position?
A: Principal at Pendleton Heights High School.

Q: And I know, from talking to you before we started, that this is your first deposition?
A: Correct.

Q: And you hope to be your last deposition?
A: Correct.

Q: Okay. Well, I'm sure your attorney told you this is just an asking/answering questions under oath.
A: Uh-huh.

Q: There is no judge here, but everything you're saying is being taken down by the court reporter. Okay?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And you're going to have to speak loudly enough for the court reporter to hear.
A: No problem.

Q: And we're going to have to make sure we don't talk over each other so that the court reporter can get everything down. Okay?
A: Okay.

Q: If at any point you don't understand my question, if I speak too fast -- I guarantee you I will not speak too slowly, but if I speak too fast or if I lapse into incoherence, let me know. Otherwise, I'll assume you understand the question. Okay?
A: Okay.

Q: If at any point you want to talk to your attorney, you, of course, can do so. The only rule is that you need to answer the question that's pending before you before you talk to the attorney. Okay?
A: Okay.

Q: I'm showing you what's been marked as Exhibit 1. Do you recognize this document?
A: Yes.

Q: And this actually is an amended document. I added a paragraph to it and sent it to your attorney last week. I added paragraph 3 on the Request for Production at the end, so I'm not sure if you saw this one. It's fine. And I apologize. I didn't change the Certificate of Service. I'm sorry. I forgot. But you are -- you recognize this as a Notice of Deposition for the principal of Pendleton Heights High School in her official capacity; is that correct?
A: Yes.

Q: And the notice asks that the principal designate one or more persons to testify on behalf of the principal as to the subjects listed in the deposition. And you have designated yourself to testify; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Lawyers. MS. PACTOR: Much to her dismay. She wishes she'd found somebody else. And how long have you been the principal at the high school?
A: This is my fourth year.

Q: And were you with the school system before then?
A: Yes.

Q: What was your -- what were your position or positions?
A: It was assistant principal. And I started in the 2008-2009 school year.

Q: At Pendleton Heights High School?
A: Correct.

Q: And prior to that were you with the South Madison Community School Corporation?
A: No.

Q: And the high school is grades 9 through 12; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And approximately how many students are enrolled?
A: Last I checked, it was 1,413.

Q: Approximately.
A: Approximately, yeah.

Q: Okay. And you understand that we're involved in a lawsuit here that claims that the Pendleton Heights Gay-Straight Alliance is not being given the same benefits as other similarly situated student clubs and organizations? Is that your understanding?
A: Yes.

Q: And I'm probably just going to lapse into saying "GSA" for the club. Is that okay?
A: Yes.

Q: And it's my understanding, from looking through the material I've seen, that the school and Corporation recognizes that there are Corporation-sponsored clubs or activities and those that are not sponsored; is that fair?
A: Correct, that there are Corporation-sponsored activities and nonCorporation activities.

Q: And sometimes I see the word or I've used the word "club" or "activity, " but it's all -- we're all talking the same thing when we mention activity. Those are groups allowed for students either because they're Corporation-sponsored or they're not Corporation-sponsored; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Okay. And I've been provided some documents from your attorney that appear -- or that are from, I assume, the South Madison Policy Manual and some from the Administrative Guideline Manual. And I'll show you what's been marked as Exhibit 2, Exhibit 3, and Exhibit 4. And I just have a general question first. Some of these, like Exhibit 4, says "Administrative Guideline Manual," whereas Exhibit 2 says "Policy Manual. " Do you know the difference between the Policy Manual and Administrative Guideline Manual?
A: No.

Q: Okay. But --
A: Say that again.

Q: I'm just asking generically if there's a distinction between the Administrative Guideline Manual and the Policy Manual. Do you see on the top of Exhibit 2 it says "Book Policy Manual," and then on Exhibit 4 it says "Book Administrative Guideline Manual"? I'm just curious to know if there's a difference between the two.
A: I'm not aware of a difference.

Q: Okay. But these are generated by the Board -- they're generated by the Board that oversees South Madison Community School Corporation; is that correct?
A: That's correct.

Q: And I guess their technical name of the School Board is the Board of Trustees of the South Madison Community School Corporation; is that correct?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And just looking at Exhibits 2, 3, and 4, these are guidelines that govern or concern both Corporation-sponsored and nonCorporation-sponsored clubs and activities. Are you aware of any other Board-generated guidelines governing Corporation-sponsored and nonCorporation-sponsored activities?
A: No.

Q: Okay.
A: That decide how a club becomes a club?

Q: And -- exactly. And differentiates between those that are Corporation-sponsored and nonCorporation- sponsored.
A: There might be policies that decide, like, how the Corporation-sponsored clubs run or how they advertise. So, like, there's -- but, no, I think these are good.

Q: Okay. But off the top of your head you're not aware of any others at this point?
A: Do you mind if I look at my notes to see if there are additional ones? I think --

Q: Of course.
A: So when I asked the question exactly what do you mean, are these the only policies that relate to clubs and organizations, is that are these the only policies that tell how a club can become a club? Because in other areas, like Student Supervision and Welfare, we have policies of how those kids in clubs and organizations are to be supervised.

Q: Okay.
A: So that's my question --

Q: Okay.
A: -- back to you.

Q: Well, usually you're not allowed to ask questions in depositions, but I deserve it. Aside from those other policies that deal with supervision once the students are in the club or activity, are you aware of any other policies or guidelines issued by the School Corporation concerning organizations and clubs?
A: There's -- 9700 is Relations with Special Interest Groups.

Q: Okay. And that governs the ability of internal club to have -- I mean a school club or organization to have connections with outside groups?
A: As well as advertisements, I think.

Q: Advertisements in the school or other advertisements?
A: In the school as well. So letter "D" is Distribution and Posting of Literature.

Q: Okay. And do you have that in front of you?
A: I do. MR. FALK: Could we go off the record, and could I look at that for just a second? MS. ROBERTS: Yes. (A discussion was held off the record.) (Deposition Exhibit 11 was marked for identification.)

Q: I'm showing you what's been marked Exhibit 11. We were talking off the record about a policy 9000 that I'm showing you as Exhibit 11. MS. ROBERTS: Is that 9700? MR. FALK: Oh, I'm sorry. THE WITNESS: Yes, 9700. And that is a policy that governs the relationship of outside groups that may have a relationship with internal school organizations; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And you had indicated, when you were talking about it before I looked at it, that it talked about advertising. Looking at it very quickly, Exhibit 11, it appears that that concerns the ability of the outside group to advertise; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Not the student organization?
A: Right.

Q: Okay. Okay. So let's go back to Exhibit 2, which you have in front of you. And this indicates it was adopted by the School Board on July 21, 2011?
A: Correct.

Q: And it's active, so it's still in effect; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And it has a definition in the third paragraph, A through D, of curricular-related activities; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And that is a definition that is used by the high school and the School Corporation to determine if a student activity is curricular-related or not curricular-related; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: I note that in the four-part definition -- and I assume that if the activity falls into any one of these four categories, it's deemed to be curricular-related; is that correct?
A: Could you repeat the question, please.

Q: Sure. Exhibit 2 defines what curricular-related activities are. And if the activity is either A, B, C or D -- just has to be one of them -- it's curricular-related; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And what is -- looking at "B," it says, "The subject matter concerns the Corporation's composite courses of study." What's a composite course of study?
A: I believe it to be the courses that we have to take to earn an Indiana diploma. So there's 40 credits that a student has to take in order to earn a high school diploma. And then, in addition to that, composite course of study, there's two other -- sorry. There are two other buckets, which is employability skills, as well as post-secondary competency. So to earn an Indiana diploma we have to have the 40 credits earned, we have to show we have employability skills in the state of Indiana, and we have to show post-secondary competencies. That's measured by test scores, the ASVAB, and scoring a 31 or higher on that, or taking the SAT and scoring a certain score on that. There's multiple other ways to fill each bucket in bucket 2 or bucket 3, but the gist of it is they have to earn 40 credits, they have to show employability skills, and then they have to show competencies for post-secondary.

Q: How do you tell if a club or activity concerns the composite courses of study?
A: If they would be related to courses that allow for a student to earn the 40 credits. So Health is a mandatory course. All students have to have that as a credit, so if we had a curricular club that relates to the standards in health and also is the curriculum that we teach in the classroom.

Q: So it has to be curriculum-related?
A: Correct.

Q: And it looks like Exhibit 3 was adopted the same day, July 21, 2011?
A: Correct.

Q: And it's still in effect as well; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And this provides for equal access for nonCorporation-sponsored clubs and activities. Is that the purpose of this provision?
A: Yes.

Q: And Exhibit 3 indicates that it's up to the principal to approve or deny nonCorporation-sponsored student clubs and activities; is that correct?
A: Yes.

Q: And that you have the final authority there; is that correct, as principal?
A: I get the ability to propose those to the School Board, and then the School Board votes on clubs that are approved or non-approved.

Q: So every club that meets at the school, whether it's curricular-related or noncurricular-related, has been approved by the School Board; is that correct?
A: Sorry. That is not correct. So every club that is a Pendleton Heights Corporation curricular club is proposed to the School Board and approved. And then non-sponsored clubs do not have access to our announcements across the board.

Q: Okay. I haven't asked you about that yet --
A: I know.

Q: -- but good to get it out. Non-sponsored means non-sponsored order by the Corporation, correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Do they have to be approved by the School Board or just by you? Just by the principal, excuse me.
A: I could -- I could allow for non-sponsored clubs to be on the announcements, like --

Q: No, I'm sorry. I'm not asking yet about announcements. I'm just asking about their existence.
A: Okay.

Q: Who approves their existence?
A: The existence of non-sponsored groups?

Q: Right.
A: No one. They're just out there. Like, they're not school-sponsored, so there could be any club that's -- sorry. I'm probably not understanding your question.

Q: Well, it's my fault. Let me start again. Let's talk about the GSA here.
A: Okay.

Q: And we'll get to it, but your lawyer gave me a piece of paper that was submitted by a faculty person to sponsor the GSA. It is a nonCorporation-sponsored club, but you signed off on it being able to meet in the school, correct?
A: Correct.

Q: So my question, now speaking generally about all -- and we'll go through which ones they are -- all nonCorporation-sponsored clubs or activities, if they're meeting in the school, do you, as principal, have to sign off on that?
A: Yes. I like to be aware of what happens in our building.

Q: Okay. And does that then get approved by the School Board, or does it stop with you saying this is a nonCorporation-sponsored club that can meet in Mrs. Smith's room Thursday after instructional time?
A: Yes, as long as it's not an organization that could have liability with it. So if there was -- for example, Pendleton Rugby might have kids that get hurt while playing, so then that does go to the Central Office so that they can collect liability insurance paperwork.

Q: But other than that, then you have the final say?
A: Yes. If it's just a meeting where we don't expect someone to get injured, then I have final say.

Q: Okay. I'm showing you what's been marked as Exhibit 4. And this is the policy or guideline from the manual that deals with Corporation-sponsored clubs and activities, correct?
A: Yes.

Q: And clubs and activities are the same thing, correct? They're student groups; is that fair?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And this is still in effect today; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And Exhibit 4, which you're looking at, talks about co-curricular and extra-curricular clubs and activities.
A: Uh-huh.

Q: What is the difference?
A: The difference between co-curricular and extra-curricular activities?

Q: Right.
A: Co-curricular is -- my understanding of co-curricular would be organizations or activities that receive a grade. So, for example, we have Choir, and they have extra-curricular activities where they perform at night. And so performing at that concert is part of their grade, so it's co-curricular. And extra-curricular activities does not link back to a grade in the curriculum.

Q: Okay. So there are Corporation-sponsored clubs, activities, groups, however you want to say that, that are both curricular and co-curricular; is that correct?
A: Yes. We have groups that are co-curricular and extra-curricular.

Q: That are Corporation-sponsored?
A: Correct.

Q: And Corporation-sponsored means that they meet one of the four characteristics noted in Exhibit 2 concerning Corporation-sponsored clubs and activities; is that correct?
A: Typically, clubs -- yes. Yes.

Q: And is there a set time during the week when Corporation-sponsored clubs, activities, groups are allowed to meet, or is it different for each activity?
A: They meet before or after school.

Q: And the same with clubs, activities or groups that you have approved that are not sponsored by the Corporation, correct?
A: Correct.

Q: You've reviewed the complaint that was filed in this case, the document that started the case?
A: Correct.

Q: And you're aware -- and, obviously, you've spoken about it briefly already, about some of the benefits that are afforded to curriculum -- or to Corporation-sponsored clubs, activities, and groups as opposed to those that are not. And we'll talk about specific clubs, but I just want to sort of finish up with what you started to talk about. If I am a Corporation-sponsored club -- which we've agreed means I meet one of the four characteristics in Exhibit 2, correct?
A: Yes.

Q: -- I'm allowed to advertise in the school; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And what kind of advertising am I doing?
A: We have our Pendleton Heights afternoon announcements, we have a few bulletin boards in our stairwells, and we have a digital electronic bulletin board.

Q: And the afternoon announcements are broadcast through the radio station, through an intercom system in the school; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And you have bulletin boards in -- there are three main stairwells; is that correct?
A: Yes. I believe that there are two bulletin boards. We have five stairwells.

Q: Okay. There are two bulletin boards over five stairwells, or there are two bulletin boards in each of the five stairwells?
A: There are two bulletin boards total.

Q: Okay.
A: Two of the five stairwells have bulletin boards.

Q: And then as you walk into the high school, there's a digital running display where you can also be advertising; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And the groups that are Corporation-sponsored are allowed, at times, to do fundraising in the school; is that correct, or on school property?
A: I'm sorry. I didn't hear your first part.

Q: The Corporation-sponsored groups are allowed to do fundraising in the school or on school property?
A: Correct, as long as it doesn't interfere with our wellness and nutrition policy.

Q: Seems to be taking a lot of fun out of it, but okay. And some of the fundraisers are selling food, I gather?
A: Yes.

Q: What other fundraisers are there?
A: We've had T-shirts sold. They've done dances.

Q: Charge admission?
A: Uh-huh.

Q: Dances at the school?
A: Correct.

Q: And there's also a Student Handbook for the high school; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And that Handbook, I know, lists clubs and organizations; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And are all the clubs and organizations listed in the Handbook those that have been or were Corporation-sponsored?
A: There is an error in the Handbook, in our current Handbook, that has not been edited.

Q: Well, let me show you -- I'm getting ahead of myself, but what the heck. I'm showing you what's been marked as Exhibit 5. And this is your current Handbook; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And the error is, I'm sorry?
A: The error is Mat Maids. Mat Maids has not existed since I was working at South Madison. MR. FALK: Can we go off the record for a second? MS. ROBERTS: Sure. (A discussion was held off the record.)

Q: Okay. Anything else besides Mat Maids that's no longer in the school?
A: I do not believe so.

Q: Okay. If you would like to start Mat Maids again, I know where you can look for --
A: A leader.

Q: A leader, yes. Okay. So the curriculum-related clubs and organizations, they're allowed to advertise; they're allowed to fundraise; they're listed in the Handbook. Are there any other benefits that they receive being a curriculum-related club, organization or group?
A: You said they're allowed to advertise. They're allowed to meet. I do not recall another benefit that they have that would be important to this conversation.

Q: Okay. Any one at all?
A: Any other benefits that they have?

Q: Right.
A: No.

Q: Okay. Now, the noncurriculum-related clubs, which you approve and are allowed to meet at the school, they also are meeting during non-instructional time; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: But they're not allowed to advertise, they're not allowed to fundraise, and they're not listed in the Handbook; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And by "not allowed to advertise" I mean not allowed to advertise on the school bulletin boards or on the digital display or through the radio station; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Now, going back to Exhibit 3, the second to the last paragraph from the bottom says that, "A student initiated group granted permission to meet on school premises shall be provided the same rights and access and shall be subject to the same administrative guidelines that govern the meetings of student organizations sponsored by this Board, except as provided by this policy." The Board-sponsored organizations that this refers to, those are the ones that we're talking about that are deemed to be curriculum-related, using the definition in Exhibit 2; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Does this policy, looking now at Exhibit 3, this paragraph, does that allow noncurriculum-related clubs to be treated differently than curriculum- related clubs?
A: Yes, I believe so. I believe that we can deny all non-sponsored clubs, but we cannot deny on the basis of the categories listed there.

Q: Okay. Now going back to Exhibit 5, I think we've established, except for the sorely departed Mat Maids, all the clubs and organizations listed in Exhibit 5 are meeting at the school at the current time; is that correct?
A: Yes.

Q: So each of these clubs and organizations were deemed to be curriculum-related, using the definition in Exhibit 2; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Okay. Now, just going through these real quickly, the Academic Club, do students receive credit for that?
A: The Academic Club?

Q: Yes.
A: No, they do not receive a credit. That is really more of -- or sorry. They do not receive a credit for that. That is where they participate against other schools in the Hoosier Heritage Conference.

Q: Right. How is that curriculum-related?
A: And so those students are recalling information from their classes. So, for example, they have a history team that competes against other schools and recalls facts that they study in World History and Euro, European history.

Q: Okay. So they're recalling information that they may have learned at school or other places as well, I assume?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay.
A: And then it also -- there's a math team, and there's a fine arts team as well that also is recalling information that they would learn in their curriculum.

Q: Or elsewhere?
A: Or elsewhere.

Q: I mean, they don't have to take certain courses to be on the Academic Club?
A: Correct.

Q: Okay. Art Club is open to people who have completed one year of high school art, but the students do not necessarily have to be in art when they're participating in the club; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And, again, they don't get credit for that; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And what is Best Buddies?
A: Best Buddies is an organization dedicated to Indiana social, physical, and economic isolation, as described in our Student Handbook.

Q: And do they get credit for participating in that?
A: They get credit for their employability skills. So, as I mentioned, we have -- a diploma in the state of Indiana has three buckets that they have to fill. So they do the 40 credits, employability skills, and the post-secondary is the third bucket. And so students do have the sponsor sign off on the employability skills when they're in certain clubs that would do activities that show leadership, organization, collaboration, any of the employability skills listed for the state of Indiana.

Q: And in Best Buddies are students --
A: Sorry. So it's not a credit as in the 40 credits, bucket 1, but it's a credit in that they have to document that they have shown employability skills.

Q: And who's showing the employability skill, the developmentally disabled student who's in Best Buddies or the non-developmentally disabled students who are participating in Best Buddies?
A: Both.

Q: And how is that employability documented?
A: The sponsor has to sign off that they did participate and gain employability skills. And that's at the discretion of the sponsor.

Q: And the sponsor is a faculty person?
A: Yes.

Q: And both -- so both the disabled and non-disabled student is getting employability documentation by the sponsor?
A: Yes.

Q: And --
A: I'm sorry. You had asked a question. I'm not sure that I answered it directly.

Q: Okay.
A: I forget what your original question was, but --

Q: We're okay.
A: Okay. It does also relate to the curriculum in other ways as well.

Q: How is that?
A: So we have special skills cadet teachers. And their role is to provide the disabled student -- they're to role model behaviors that would be appropriate. And those are English language art skills, the speaking and listening skills, as well as vocabulary skills. It would be vocabulary that they may sometimes not hear in a secluded classroom.

Q: And what is that related to?
A: The cadet teachers is a program that we have. Cadet teachers is similar to -- well, not similar to. It's the same, but we have a cadet teacher that may go into a regular elementary classroom, and we have cadet teachers that go into our central skills classroom, which pertains to a lot of our students that are in Best Buddies. We also have cadets that are unable to fill the cadet teacher role because they have a hefty academic schedule, so there's just not room in their schedule to do cadet teaching during the day. So then that provides them the opportunity to mentor the special ed students during the Best Buddies time, during the group meeting. We also have -- with the Best Buddies and talking about the employability skills, the planning, the events that they have, we have a Thanksgiving, or a Friendsgiving, where Best Buddies -- the special needs student and regular ed student meet, and the regular ed student helps them with cooking skills, which would relate to our family and consumer science programs that we have.

Q: And are all the students who are non-developmentally disabled in Best Buddies, are they all cadet teachers?
A: No.

Q: And it's not required they be so to be in Best Buddies; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And how frequently does Best Buddies meet with each other?
A: That's a good question. We just came off of a year where most --

Q: Sure.
A: -- groups did not meet. I know that they have five dominant activities that they perform, and I could not tell you the number of times that they meet to make that event run smoothly.

Q: And are Best Buddies paired one-on-one?
A: Yes, they like to be paired one-on-one. I can't say that they are always paired one-on-one if there's a shortage on one end or the other.

Q: And you said that they get -- their sponsor can, if they do okay, can deem that to have met some of the employability skills requirement?
A: Yes.

Q: And what is that requirement for a non-developmentally disabled person? What would they have to do in order to graduate?
A: On the employability skills?

Q: Yes.
A: They could do a variety of different things. The kids can earn their employability skills by actually having a job. So a boss at any workplace can sign off on that. Our athletes receive credit for the employability skills if they play a sport. So that's in regards to time management, collaboration, teamwork are some of the employability skills listed there. And then the employability skills are signed off on by our sponsors for multiple clubs that we have.

Q: And is there an hour requirement for that? Or how do you meet that at the time of graduation? How do you know you've satisfied your employability skill requirement?

Q: Is there a concern that if you propose the GSA as an official club, that there might be some sort of counter-club that you'd have to recognize because of your concern about neutrality?
A: No.

Q: So what is the impediment today to requesting that the GSA be a -- become an official club?
A: What would they have to do to become an official club?

Q: Sure.
A: They would need to write a proposal and show that they can have sustainability. And then we'd have to analyze how that fits into our curriculum. And then, ultimately, the School Board gets to decide those that are proposed.

Q: But, as of today, you're unwilling to commit to allowing -- to proposing them because of your concern about the past history and the sporadic nature of the club; is that correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And what would they have to do to overcome that, in your estimation?
A: I would like to see more curricular connections with it, not just coming up in times of controversy, so that I know that kids are gaining something related to the academics out of it.

Q: And the controversy you referred to is the controversy over the teachers not allowed to post -- I think there were flags or LGBTQ-supporting information in the classroom; is that correct?
A: Right. I would just like to see them sustain for support for each other versus just coming and going, electing leaders that elect new officers at the end of the year and then they carry it over into the next year. And they've not been able to sustain themselves.

Q: But you agree that if they could advertise in the school and spread the word around about their existence as an official club, that would help attract students; is that fair?
A: No.

Q: Why?
A: We have other groups that are nonCorporation- sponsored, that don't advertise in school and have sustained their existence as well as their membership. Because of today's world we have social media. We have multiple other ways to advertise.

Q: You don't think being able to advertise and being able to be known as an official club, being in the Student Handbook, would be beneficial to any club, in terms of its support?
A: I'm not saying whether it would or would not be beneficial to it. I can tell you that there are clubs that do not get advertised that have a large membership base.

Q: Sure.
A: So it could help them, it could not help them. But I guess to say that that is a factor that has been detrimental to them I do not believe is the case because we have clubs in our community that don't get to advertise that have a large membership.

Q: But the LGBTQ students might feel very marginalized. Not just in this high school but in any high school; is that fair?
A: I can't speak to how they feel.

Q: Okay. Is there a school newspaper?
A: The Muse is a publication. And we used to have HoofPrints, but it does not exist anymore.

Q: And does the Muse have advertisements in it?
A: No.

Q: Okay. And does the school have an official -- any official social media accounts that official clubs have access to for purposes of advertising or announcements?
A: Yes.

Q: What does the school have?
A: So WEEM promotes a lot of our activities.

Q: WEEM is the radio station?
A: Radio station. And I can't say whether they have or have not promoted our Pendleton Heights Corporation-sponsored clubs, but they could. I mean, if there was -- they could retweet something from one of those groups and probably, I would guess, probably have, but I don't know that for sure.

Q: Okay. And at the beginning of the deposition you talked about the composite course of study, which is equivalent to the Core 40; is that fair? Or is that different than the Core 40?
A: I assume the composite course of study means how high school students earn a diploma, which is an Indiana diploma requirement.

Q: Okay.
A: And so that's our 40 credits, the employability skills, and the post-secondary competencies.

Q: And the 40 credits, are they -- it's been a while since my kids graduated high school. Are the 40 credits in particular courses or any courses?
A: No particular courses. So you have to get eight English language arts credits. I don't know all of them by heart.

Q: That's fair.
A: But each category is broken down into course subjects, Science, Math, Social Studies, and English. And then you have elective credits that you have to earn and others.

Q: But there's some electives you may take that may not go to your composite course of study; is that right?
A: Correct. We have students that graduate with 50-plus credits, so they do not need all of the credits they take to earn a high school diploma. MR. FALK: Okay. I have nothing further. Thank you very much. THE WITNESS: Thank you. MS. ROBERTS: I have just a couple of questions. EXAMINATION, QUESTIONS BY MS. ROBERTS:

Q: It's been a while ago in your deposition when we went through the list of clubs that are shown in Exhibit 5, I believe.
A: Yes.

Q: I want to -- there were a couple they went through very quickly, but I want to make sure that we've got everything we need here from your testimony. You talked about Beta and the National Honor Society?
A: Uh-huh.

Q: And I recall that you said those relate generally to scholarship and promoting good scholarship. Do those clubs have other curricular connections?
A: Yes. Within the second bucket of the Indiana diploma there's employability skills, and those are broken down into three sections. And one of those sections are service-based learning. And so for service-based learning, National Honor Society and Beta provides the kids opportunities to do service-based for our community.

Q: When you say this is in bucket 2, is that bucket something that all students are required to fill or have checked off in order to graduate?
A: Yes.

Q: What sort of service-based learning does Beta or National Honor Society do?
A: They do a variety. National Beta Club might go out in our community and help with our tornados that we had back in 2018. National Honor Society could fall in that same category. So any group that is in need in our community or surrounding. They might collect water and send it down to New Orleans for the hurricane. Basically, any need that arises would be an opportunity for the students in National Beta Club and National Honor Society to fulfill the hours that they have to earn to be in the club. So they have service hours, and I don't know the number of service hours per group. But any opportunity that arises where a group is in need, they may go out and do that and then turn that in to their sponsor.

Q: Okay. So the Beta or National Honor Society itself may have a set number of service hours, but for Indiana's graduation criteria it's not a set number of hours. It's just simply doing something to demonstrate that you've done service-based learning and having someone sign off on it?
A: Correct.

Q: And so if someone meets their service hours in Beta, then that person -- their sponsor would then sign off saying that they have fulfilled bucket 2 of the Indiana graduation requirement?
A: Right. Which could be those employability skills or service-based learning.

Q: So before a sponsor were to sign off on that, it could be that -- I think you talked about employability skills, including time management, organization. I don't recall everything you talked about.
A: Yes.

Q: But for a sponsor to sign off, would Beta or National Honor Society satisfy those items as well?
A: Correct. And then -- so sometimes students don't fulfill their service hours, and so they don't get signed off on in Beta and National Honor Society. So they would either have to stay in Beta another year and maybe fulfill it that way or go get a job to fulfill that bucket 2 in another route.

Q: Okay. And just to be clear, Beta and National Honor Society both, based upon the sort of service-based projects they do, satisfies bucket 2 either because of employability or because of service-based learning?
A: Correct. MS. ROBERTS: Okay. I don't have any other questions. FURTHER EXAMINATION, QUESTIONS BY MR. FALK:

A: Correct. So --

Q: What's bucket 3?
A: Post-secondary competency skills. So showing that you are prepared to go to some type of post-secondary, so military, college. You don't -- they also take things like how many AP courses that you take and that you got a "C" or above in those as well.

Q: Okay.
A: And so employability skills can be covered through project-based learning, service-based learning, or work-based learning. So the work-based is the employability. The service-based is the clubs that we have that provide services or volunteer hours. Project-based learning can be certain courses that we have where they produce a product in that class.

A: Correct.

Q: Is there anything that would prevent you from proposing that the GSA be an official club, be a curriculum-related club?

Q: Is there any other reason not to propose them as an official club?
A: No.

Q: And there have been clubs that have been recognized as official in the past, like Mat Maids, which have ceased to exist; is that correct?

Sometimes that's budget cuts and funding, because we pay a stipend to the sponsors. So I have to be selective when I choose groups. So, for example, over my time as principal I've had someone want to have a dance club, which could also be related to the PE curriculum or the fine arts. I've had a kid just this year that wanted to do a men's volleyball club. That could be related to athletics that we already have or the physical education curriculum. So I do have to consider my goals as a principal and what I want to promote. And so sometimes being cross-curricular helps. Like, the e-Sports is -- provides kids with a lot of lucrative jobs beyond high school. So what I'm trying to say is there could be many clubs that people bring to me that I could propose to the Board. So I have to analyze which ones I want to take that I think can be fruitful and meet the needs of the students at Pendleton Heights High School.
